chapter: New York and the Lloyd quartet
title: Playing with Rashied Ali: no rehearsal and multidirectional time
summary: No rehearsal at the Plugged Nickel; he learns from Rashied Ali and Andrew Cyrille's multidirectional drumming.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Was that just a one week gig?
One week, and did anybody else talk to you in so far as the music or concepts, suggestions, concepts, anything?
No, we'd just get up and play.
So no rehearsal, he hired you for the gig…
How about any discussion or dialogue between you and Rashied about?

Not really, we just hit it. Because Rashied knew the book and just created the motion. He'd create this multi-direction motion, which was fantastic. Andrew Cyrille knows how to do that too, does that well. I heard him with Cecil Taylor and it's a kind of playing; it's not for everybody. You have to… …I could sit there and appreciate it. If you don't come at that music with an attitude about what music is and just come with an open… …you start to hear the validity of it.
